post.0:
I won 111 to Cal's 94, and the whole game came down to one round III decision: taking Last Call on my first placement, which pushed my other four minions to after everyone else was out. With every rival out of minions I could count exactly, and Dilute, Promote, Sleep In and Trade Seeds plus Closer's +4 purple took all four +10 contests by margins of one (6-5 red, 5-3 purple, 4-3 silver, 3-2 yellow). That was a 40-point swing, and Cal, who had been running away at 95 off Promote/Demote rival swaps, Largesse and buy-10s, had no answer because his turns were already spent. Before that I was losing: Cal's Promote and Demote took my Deprogrammers and Line Cutters in round II and HR in round III, so the win rests almost entirely on the closing seat, not on how I played rounds I and II. Everyone cashing out to zero with buy-10s in round III left the contests cheap for whoever moved last. Honestly it felt more like an exploit of turn order than a hard-fought win.

META: The contests are the heart of the game and the color tricks around them (Dilute, Hold Up, Trade Seeds, Pocket Watch) are fun and tense. What isn't working is that buy-10 makes most members a worse deal than cashing out, so round III turns into everyone dumping their piles to zero, and then whoever places last (Last Call, or Line Cutters/snake ends) takes all four +10 contests for almost nothing. Promote and Demote offering rival-to-rival and wide cost gaps, combined with Recruiter and Deprogrammers, was the biggest feel-bad of the night. First change: make Promote/Demote only swap your own member within the printed cost range, then look at Last Call in round III.
post.1:
I came last with 73, and it was decided before round III started, when Ava took Last Call and got four placements after everyone else had finished. I won yellow in rounds I and II with Guest Book, Dyer and denying the yellow spaces, but in round III I couldn't hold a contest without giving up followers I'd otherwise buy, and anything I held, she could beat from the last seat. My one real attempt, keeping 8 red, got Diluted down to 5 and then topped with Promote plus Trade Seeds. I also wasted a buy on Tastemaker because I read it as +1 per resource changed when it's +1 per Dilute. Overall I played the efficient line, but the big swings at this table (Party Gifts, Largesse, Walk-In, the Red swaps, Last Call) mostly came from spaces, not engines, and I took too few of them.

META: The core of the game works: the hold-versus-spend tension on contests is real and interesting in rounds I and II, and the colors feel different. In round III a recruit is worth 10 followers and the contests are worth 10, so whoever places last with the most placements wins the contests, and Last Call hands that seat to one player. The biggest swings came from flat spaces (Party Gifts, Largesse, Walk-In) and the Red swaps, not from engines. First fix: limit Promote and Demote to swapping your own member, as printed, then look at Last Call in round III.

I came second on 94 to Ava's 111. I led most of the game off Party Gifts, Red's swap spaces, Largesse and buying 10s, and I was 85 to Dee's 88 going into the last placements with a tie in my favor. What decided it was Ava's round III Last Call: she placed the last four minions after everyone was out and took all four +10 contests on 4-6 of each color, which is 40 followers from one space choice. I helped her: my Philanthropists and Largesse silver went to her because Dee owned silver, and a misclick on Con Men stole Dee's purple instead of Ben's yellow, which handed Ava purple. I didn't see the Last Call sweep coming until it was too late, and my last minion couldn't have stopped four contests anyway; the only real counter was taking Last Call myself on my round III double.

META: The contest prizes and buying 10s dwarf most members by round III; the game came down to who held the last placements, and Last Call let one player go last four times and sweep 40 followers. The gift spaces (Party Gifts, Largesse, Philanthropists) are fun, but they pay the giver a lot, and the silver has to land on whoever isn't fighting the silver leader. Red's swap spaces are the most interesting decisions on the wheel, but the options list went far beyond the printed 'costing up to 2 more/less' and offered rival-to-rival swaps. First change: cap Last Call (for example 'skip your next two turns' instead of 'until everyone else is out') so the +10 contests can't all be swept by one closing run.

I finished third on 88. My silver engine (Caterer, Toastmaster, Toast every round, Debt Collectors straight after a Toast, Debutantes doubling to 26) worked and won silver in rounds I and II, but in round III I couldn't hold any contest because Ava had the last four placements after Last Call. The moment that decided the game was Ava's Last Call at the start of round III: from then on every contest was hers if she wanted it, and she took all four for +40 on her last four minions. I made the right call to cash my silver into followers instead of defending it, but that meant my round III was capped at 10 per recruit, and recruits ran out before resources did. Earlier I also misread purple in round II: my own Sleep In plus Ava's Hold Up on me fed her Pocket Watch three purple and I only got a tie.

META: The contests are the heart of the game and the moment-to-moment reads (Dilute, Toast, Sleep In to move your last minion) are genuinely good. What isn't working: round III is decided by turn order, not by what you built: Last Call hands one player four closing placements against +10 contests, and buying followers 10 at a time makes recruits the only limit, so engines matter less than tempo. Promote and Demote offering rival-to-rival swaps (with Recruiter paying) created the runaway leader and should be fixed first; after that I'd cap or rethink Last Call in round III.
